title: Record how far rejected alternatives got
acceptance: Each decision accepts an optional `rejected` list of objects `{option: string, how_far: one of "discussed" | "prototyped" | "built_then_removed", note: optional string}`; `Checkpoint.from_dict` accepts it and `to_dict` round-trips it unchanged (pytest test)
A decision with no `rejected` key, `rejected: null` or `rejected: []` loads and round-trips with an empty list (pytest test)

Invalid input fails with ValidationError naming the exact field: unknown `how_far` value (e.g. "tried") -> `decisions[0].rejected[0].how_far`; empty or missing `option` -> `decisions[0].rejected[0].option`; `rejected` not a list -> `decisions[0].rejected` (pytest tests)

`render_brief` lists each rejected alternative under its decision with its option and how far it got in readable words (e.g. `Rejected: hooks (prototyped)` and `built, then removed`), plus the note when present, so a resumed chat can answer 'was X ever tried?' (pytest asserts the strings appear)
The save_checkpoint schema/description in schema.py documents the `rejected` field and its allowed `how_far` values (`get` of the registered tool's input schema shows them)
Secrets inside `option` or `note` (e.g. `sk-ant-...`, `token=abcd1234efgh`) are stored redacted by `Store.save` (pytest test)

Old-format checkpoints still work: a test fixture shaped like cp-001..cp-003 (decisions with only `decision` and `reason`, no `workspace`) loads via `Store.get`, resumes via the MCP `resume_checkpoint` tool and the CLI, and its rendered brief is byte-identical to a golden file captured from the pre-change code (pytest test)

title: Workspace section and 'set up first' checklist on resume
acceptance: Checkpoints accept an optional `workspace` object covering ROADMAP item 8: files/folders (path), repos (path, branch, last_commit), access granted (folders, permissions such as delete/push), connectors/MCP servers, tools and setup (venv/interpreter, CLIs, local servers/ports), env vars by NAME only, skills/plugins/agents, and external references (URL/doc/ticket/artifact); every item carries a status of `still_relevant` or `done_with`. `from_dict`/`to_dict` round-trip a fully populated workspace (pytest test)

A missing or null `workspace`, or one with only some categories, loads with empty defaults; an item with an unknown status (e.g. "maybe") or a missing path/name fails with ValidationError naming the field, e.g. `workspace.repos[0].status` (pytest tests)

Env vars are names only: an env var entry given as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-abc123...` is stored as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with no value anywhere in the saved JSON file (pytest test reads the file on disk)
Secrets anywhere in workspace strings (tokens in URLs, `Bearer ...`, `password=...`) are redacted in the saved file by `Store.save` (pytest test)

`render_brief` for a checkpoint with still-relevant workspace items shows a short 'Set up first' checklist (before 'Before you continue') listing only `still_relevant` items (folders to request, connectors to check, repo + branch + last commit, tools/env var names, files to open); `done_with` items do not appear in the checklist (pytest test)
That brief tells the resumed AI to ask the user before requesting any folder access or connector, not to assume it (pytest asserts the instruction text)
When there is no workspace, or every item is `done_with`, the brief has no 'Set up first' checklist (pytest test)

The save_checkpoint description in schema.py asks the saving AI to fill `workspace`, judge each item still relevant or done with, and give env var names never values; the pinned hash and length constants in tests/test_eval.py are updated to the new text with a comment saying why, and both hash tests pass

The same old-format fixture still renders a byte-identical brief after this feature, and `$HOME/aic-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` from the repo root reports 0 failures with the 117 previously passing tests still present
